summary: This JUnit test checks the thermostat's printStatusToDisplay() method by temporarily redirecting System.out into a buffer, so the text the method prints can be captured and compared against the expected line.

lines.text: A ByteArrayOutputStream collects bytes in memory instead of sending them to the screen, which is what makes the printed output inspectable.
System.out is a PrintStream, so a replacement one must be built from this class.
A static import lets the test call assertEquals directly rather than writing Assertions.assertEquals every time.
The book uses this placeholder to show that the earlier tests in this class stay where they are; only the new test is being added.
The method name states the behaviour under test, so a failure report reads like a sentence about what broke.
A thermostat at 72 degrees with eco mode off is comfortable, so its status should be Idle.
Saving the real System.out first is essential, because the test must put it back or every later test loses its output.
From this point on, anything printed with System.out.println lands in the buffer instead of the console.
This is the call under test; its only visible effect is the text it prints.
A finally block runs whether the call succeeds or throws, which guarantees the next line always executes.
Restoring the original stream undoes the global change so the test leaves no side effects behind.
println appends the platform's line ending, so System.lineSeparator() is added to the expected text to keep the test passing on Windows as well as Linux and macOS.
